name: "Artist - Topic" channels / Official Artist Channel (OAC) badge
type: Classifier (near-binary, high precision) + identifier — channel-name/badge heuristic that simultaneously flags music and supplies the artist name directly
maintainer: Google/YouTube auto-generates Topic channels from the Content ID / YouTube Music ingestion pipeline; the Official Artist Channel program is Google-operated but nomination-gated — requests only come from labels, distributors, or Music Service Partners, not self-serve by the artist.
method: Metadata parsing/heuristic: check the uploading channel's display title for the literal suffix ' - Topic' (marking an auto-generated, audio-ingestion-only distributor channel), or check the channel header's badge renderer for the Official Artist Channel music-note verified-artist badge; when the '- Topic' suffix matches, the channel title with that suffix stripped is used directly as the artist string.
required_input: Channel title/handle text and, for the OAC path, badge metadata — obtainable from whichever transport already supplies channel context (ytInitialData HTML, Innertube /next channel header, or Data API channels.list snippet.title). No audio, no extra video-level fetch beyond what's already retrieved for other purposes.
classification_or_hitrate: Widely cited as near-100% precision for 'uploaded by a music-artist Topic channel implies this is music' — but the '- Topic' auto-generation mechanism is not exclusively used for music: YouTube also auto-generates Topic channels for other audio content such as podcasts, so the bare suffix check alone is not a pure music signal and should be paired with confirmation that the channel represents a music artist (e.g. cross-checked against the video actually carrying music-panel/Art Track data) rather than trusted in isolation. [uncertain] Recall is inherently capped: this signal only fires for content actually distributed through YouTube Music/Content-ID ingestion pipelines — self-uploaded indie music, cover/karaoke channels, and live-performance uploads on ordinary (non-Topic) channels never trigger it even though they are unambiguously music.
pitch_speed_cover_robustness: Robust in a different sense than audio-fingerprint methods: channel identity is entirely independent of audio content, so it never misfires due to nightcore/speed/pitch edits — but by the same token it provides zero coverage when a nightcore or sped-up reupload is posted by an unrelated reuploader channel rather than the original Topic channel, even though the underlying song is unchanged. Strong on precision, weak on recall for edited/reuploaded audio.
catalog_language_bias: Topic channels are auto-generated for essentially any artist whose music is ingested into YouTube's Content ID / YouTube Music catalog, spanning Western, K-pop, J-pop, and C-pop content reasonably well since most digital distributors (CD Baby, Believe, TuneCore, DistroKid, etc.) route ingestion through this same pipeline globally; coverage is comparatively broader across regions/genres than the engagement-panel signal, but still weak for artists who never signed with any digital aggregator/distributor — bedroom/indie producers, doujin circles, and anime insert songs uploaded directly by a label's branded (non-Topic) channel fall outside this signal entirely. [uncertain]
evaluation_dataset: None published by Google; the 'near 100% precision' characterization is a widely repeated community/heuristic claim (reverse-engineering communities, music-tech blogs, yt-dlp-adjacent discussions) rather than a measured benchmark against a labeled dataset.
confidence_calibration: Effectively binary — either the channel title ends in ' - Topic' or carries the OAC badge, or it doesn't; no numeric score, though the binary match itself can reasonably be treated as a fixed high-confidence flag once triggered.
api_availability: Free — channel title/badge data rides on whatever transport is already fetching channel context (ytInitialData HTML, Innertube, or the free-tier-quota Data API's channels.list); no separate paid service is required specifically for this check.
chrome_extension_usability: Trivial client-side string check on data the extension already has for other purposes (channel name is always present in page/video metadata); no extra network call, no additional CORS/host_permissions concern beyond whatever transport already supplies the channel context.
client_vs_server: Entirely local string comparison; no additional data leaves the client beyond whatever channel metadata was already fetched incidentally for other purposes.
bundle_weight_cold_start: Negligible — a string-suffix check or small badge lookup, effectively 0ms marginal cost.
breakage_risk: Low for the naming convention itself — the '<Artist> - Topic' pattern has been a stable, long-lived convention since the Google Play Music/YouTube Music Topic-channel rollout years ago and is well documented across the music-distribution industry (RouteNote, TuneCore, Ditto Music, Unchained guides all describe it consistently). Moderate risk on the OAC-badge field's exact API location, which — like Items 2/3 — lives in unversioned renderer JSON subject to redesign. A slower-moving structural risk: Google is actively encouraging artists to merge Topic channels into unified Official Artist Channels, which could gradually reduce how many active artists still present the literal '- Topic' suffix as their video's uploader over time, shifting reliance toward the OAC badge path instead. [uncertain]
realtime_capability: Yes, effectively instant — a string check with no network round-trip of its own.
identification_fields: artist, extracted directly from the channel title (minus the ' - Topic' suffix), plus a near-certain music-content flag; does not by itself supply song title, album, or ISRC — must be paired with video-title parsing or the description/panel signals (Items 2/3/5) for the actual song title.
tos_restrictions: Reading a channel's already-public display name/badge carries the same general ToS caveat as whatever transport delivers it (none if sourced via the official Data API's channels.list; the general unofficial-scraping caveat if sourced via ytInitialData/Innertube) — the data point itself (a public channel name) carries no special restriction beyond its transport.
risk_tolerance_note: Same risk bucket as Items 2/3 if sourced via HTML/Innertube; zero additional risk if the channel title is instead pulled via the fully official Data API channels.list endpoint for this specific field.
cascade_position: Gate — very cheap and very high precision, well suited as an early high-confidence gate to short-circuit further audio-based classification/fingerprinting once a Topic-channel or OAC match is found; naturally complements Items 2/5 for the actual song-title extraction once the music/artist determination is made.
failure_mode: Fails silently in the common case (no channel-name match simply produces no signal, falling through to the next pipeline stage) — the more consequential risk is a false positive if the '- Topic' check is applied too loosely and matches a non-music Topic channel (e.g. a podcast auto-generated Topic channel), which would produce a confidently-wrong music classification, a visible product defect for a karaoke overlay. [uncertain]
cost_model_at_scale: $0 — no dedicated API call; rides entirely on whatever transport already supplies the channel name for other purposes.
geo_region_availability: Topic-channel generation is tied to the same Content-ID/label-ingestion pipeline as Items 2/3, subject to territory-by-territory licensing variability in which catalogs get ingested at all, but once a Topic channel or OAC badge exists it is globally visible metadata, unlike engagement-panel presence which can be region-gated per individual viewer.
